bug_semantics: In a server-capable NextChat deployment, app/mcp/actions.ts has a file-level "use server" directive, so its exported async MCP-management functions are remotely invocable Next.js Server Actions. The first exploitable form exposed updateMcpConfig, which accepted and persisted a caller-controlled MCP command/args/env configuration, and restartAllClients, which reloaded that configuration and passed it to StdioClientTransport; an unauthenticated caller could invoke those client-bundled actions in sequence to spawn an arbitrary process. Commit 8aa9a500fdee762abe5fd8e0bba00065be1725f4 later consolidated the same unsafe trust boundary into the advisory-named addMcpServer action, making arbitrary command execution a single request. No authentication, authorization, effective ENABLE_MCP gate, command allowlist, or safe environment boundary protects that action path; static-export builds do not expose Server Actions.
flaw_origin: The smallest real BIC is 7d51bfd42e0f60a328abed353ab1ef717b6f3ba8 ("feat: MCP market"), not the later addMcpServer refactor. It first changed MCP configuration from a repository-owned static JSON import to caller-writable state and simultaneously exported the updateMcpConfig and restartAllClients Server Actions that turn an untrusted ServerConfig into a spawned stdio process. The immediate parent could initialize only repository-shipped configurations and had neither of those attacker-controlled management actions. The later 8aa9a500fdee762abe5fd8e0bba00065be1725f4 optimization replaced the two-action route with addMcpServer but did not originate the unauthenticated command-execution trust failure.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file commit 7d51bfd42e0f60a328abed353ab1ef717b6f3ba8 shows author and committer Kadxy <2230318258@qq.com> and only the message "feat: MCP market"; it contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-assistance trailer, bot identity, or other AI marker.
evidence: First-party disclosure https://github.com/ChatGPTNextWeb/NextChat/issues/6757 identifies the public addMcpServer Server Action in app/mcp/actions.ts, explains that caller-controlled command and args reach StdioClientTransport in app/mcp/client.ts, confirms unauthenticated RCE on 2.16.1, distinguishes server-capable deployments from static export, and states that ENABLE_MCP is not enforced on the action. GHSA-2jqp-6hx7-phh8 / CVE-2026-7644 reports versions through 2.16.1 affected and says the project had not responded.

In the validated clone, git log --all -S 'export async function updateMcpConfig' -- app/mcp/actions.ts and git log -L :updateMcpConfig:app/mcp/actions.ts 7d51bfd42e0f60a328abed353ab1ef717b6f3ba8 both identify 7d51bfd42e0f60a328abed353ab1ef717b6f3ba8 as the first writer. The BIC adds file-level Server Action updateMcpConfig(config), which writes JSON.stringify(config) to app/mcp/mcp_config.json, and restartAllClients(), which clears state and calls initializeMcpClients(); that initializer reads the now-writable file and calls createClient(serverConfig, clientId). git log -L :restartAllClients:app/mcp/actions.ts at the BIC likewise begins at this commit.

git show 7d51bfd42e0f60a328abed353ab1ef717b6f3ba8:app/components/mcp-market.tsx shows both updateMcpConfig and restartAllClients imported into the client component and saveConfig calling them sequentially, making their Server Action identifiers client-visible. app/mcp/client.ts already passes ServerConfig.command, args, and env to StdioClientTransport and connects it, which is the process-spawn sink.

Direct parent verification: git grep -n -e updateMcpConfig -e restartAllClients -e addMcpServer 0c14ce6417821d512d04dec5a5755bf35deed51d -- app returns no matches. git show 0c14ce6417821d512d04dec5a5755bf35deed51d:app/mcp/actions.ts instead imports repository-owned mcp_config.json and initializes only Object.entries(conf.mcpServers); it has no action accepting an attacker-supplied ServerConfig and no caller-triggerable restart after a config write. Thus the exploitable configuration-to-spawn path is absent from the immediate parent.

Lifecycle cross-check: git show 8aa9a500fdee762abe5fd8e0bba00065be1725f4 -- app/mcp/actions.ts app/mcp/client.ts shows the later large 'Optimize MCP configuration logic' commit replacing the exported write/restart route with exported addMcpServer(clientId, config), which persists config and immediately calls initializeSingleClient. git log -S 'addMcpServer' -- app/mcp/actions.ts begins there. Commit e440ff56c89d11b29cdbb303eb8a9a71cddc2553 later amplified secret exposure by merging process.env into the spawned transport environment. Commit bc71ae247bd1110658aef933eaf301b344181122 only added isMcpEnabled as a separate exported query and did not call it from addMcpServer.

Release boundary: git tag --contains 7d51bfd42e0f60a328abed353ab1ef717b6f3ba8 returns exactly v2.16.0 and v2.16.1. git merge-base --is-ancestor confirms the BIC is in v2.16.0 (tag object resolves to 377480b448798488db5ef03f4d5c44d2d930693c) but not v2.15.8; v2.15.8 has none of the MCP management symbols, while git grep at both v2.16.0 and v2.16.1 finds exported addMcpServer in app/mcp/actions.ts. This makes v2.16.0 the first tagged affected release and v2.15.8 the last earlier tag.

No closing fix exists in public upstream history as of 2026-08-28. origin/main and git ls-remote origin HEAD both resolve to defdcdb55d850cd12c4c657eb83729fd66e215c0; at that tree git grep finds exported addMcpServer at app/mcp/actions.ts:164, isMcpEnabled only as a separate function at line 377, config.command at app/mcp/client.ts:16, and full process.env inheritance at line 20. git log --all -- app/mcp/actions.ts has no security change after January 2025, and issue #6757 remains open with a 2026-08-28 comment asking when it will be fixed. Therefore fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are null rather than guessed.

BIC-only AI check: git cat-file commit 7d51bfd42e0f60a328abed353ab1ef717b6f3ba8 yields tree c803595e66f0415926d75e08c452a32ddd3d6e60, parent 0c14ce6417821d512d04dec5a5755bf35deed51d, human author/committer Kadxy <2230318258@qq.com>, and the single-line message 'feat: MCP market', with no trailers or bot identity. No later commit, issue text, or fix-side signal is used for the verdict.
reasoning: The advisory spotlights the one-request addMcpServer form, but treating its January 15 optimization as the BIC would mistake a later consolidation for the origin. On January 9, 7d51bfd42e0f60a328abed353ab1ef717b6f3ba8 first crossed the critical trust boundary: unauthenticated client-visible Server Actions could persist arbitrary command configuration and then force the server to instantiate it. The parent had a server-side MCP subsystem but only repository-owned command configuration, so the attacker-controlled source-to-spawn path is directly absent there. The January 15 addMcpServer change shortened the exploit from two actions to one, the environment change increased impact, and ENABLE_MCP added a UI/config query without enforcing authorization; none is an earlier origin or a fix. Tagged releases v2.16.0 and v2.16.1 contain the flaw, and current upstream main remains vulnerable. Finally, the BIC commit object has no explicit AI attribution or bot identity, so under the required BIC-only standard the correct closed verdict is NOT_AI even though the vulnerability is still unpatched.
remaining_gap: Unpatched upstream as of 2026-08-28: no fix commit or first patched release exists to record; fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are intentionally null.
